partA.missionPremise: Operator-observed production defect 2026-09-15: searching 48209:97652 rendered a brief titled 'Parcel 97651'; the Reports/Exports panel then refused with 'Export target 48209:97651 is not the selected property (48209:97652).' The dispatch states the serve layer is cleared (each id's direct read returns its own matching apn) and frames the defect as client-side selection state.

codeReadingFindings.confirmedMechanism: Two DIFFERENT client-side stores track 'the current parcel', maintained by disjoint code paths with NO reconciliation between them: (1) subjectStore (apps/property-explorer/src/lib/subject-store.ts), written only by setSubjectByParcelNodeId, guarded by ONE unified monotonic generation counter (subjectWriteGeneration) so a slower earlier resolve can never overwrite a later one -- this is the store export-target.ts's resolveExportTarget checks against, and it is thoroughly tested (subject-store.test.ts, 'does not let a slower earlier resolve overwrite a later call'). (2) The rendered card (ExplorerMap.tsx's cardNodeId/inspectedRef state), written by inspectInPlace at five independent call sites (search-pending L1087, search-sealed L1143, live-GIS click L1480, bare-overlay click L1500, PMTiles click L1542), each guarded by its OWN ad hoc mechanism (lookupIntentRef.current.isCurrent(...) for the search path, a direct inspectedRef.current?.parcelNodeId comparison inside adoptSubject's .then() for the click path) -- and nothing calls back from subjectStore to the card. The exported/displayed 'active parcel' (activeParcelNodeId = cardNodeId ?? subjectNodeId, feeding the Reports/Exports panel and the brief title) is sourced from this SECOND, weakly-guarded state, not from subjectStore directly.
codeReadingFindings.traceDepth: Manually traced every one of the five inspectInPlace call sites against every other (search-vs-search via lookupIntentRef re-bump; click-vs-search via adoptSubject's own lookupIntentRef.bump() at its top; the subjectWriteGeneration cross-check inside setSubjectByParcelNodeId) using the exact 'slower earlier resolve' interleaving subject-store.test.ts proves safe at the subjectStore layer. Each of the five call sites is individually well-guarded against every interleaving I could construct against ITS OWN counterpart paths. I could NOT reproduce a fully deterministic minimal repro purely from those five call sites with certainty from static reading alone -- reported honestly rather than fabricating a specific trigger I have not verified (DEV_PROCESS 3.2/3.2a). What IS certain, and independent of which exact interleaving the operator hit: nothing in the architecture prevents the two stores from disagreeing once ANY guard (present or a future one added at a sixth call site) has a gap, because there is no reconciliation step. This is the actionable defect regardless of the precise trigger.
codeReadingFindings.rejectedAlternativeMechanism: A server/API defect returning the wrong record for a requested id. REJECTED per the dispatch's own pre-dispatch check: a direct read of 48209:97650/97651/97652/97658 each returns its own matching apn -- the binding is correct at the API, and I did not re-derive or re-run that check since the dispatch states it was already run and the client-side divergence (subjectStore correct, card wrong) is inconsistent with a server-side mislabel (a server mislabel would make BOTH the card and subjectStore wrong identically, since both ultimately read the same resolver.resolve(id) result for whichever id each call was actually given).

designDecision.chosen: Make the rendered card a PROJECTION of subjectStore BY CONSTRUCTION rather than searching for and patching one more ad hoc guard at whichever call site the operator's exact click sequence exploited. New module apps/property-explorer/src/lib/card-subject-guard.ts exports a pure reconcileCardWithSubject(inspectedParcelNodeId, fallbackAddress, subject, buildCard) -> {parcelNodeId, card} | null. ExplorerMap.tsx subscribes to subjectStore and applies it on every change, calling the EXISTING inspectInPlace with the reconciled card whenever the two disagree.
designDecision.whyThisClosesBothFalsifiers: Falsifier 1 (fixing only the refusal message) is not in play -- no message text was touched; the brief itself is corrected. Falsifier 2 (export target still independently settable) is closed because the export's expectedParcelNodeId is sourced from cardNodeId, and cardNodeId is now forced to converge on subjectStore's id on every subjectStore change -- the two cannot stay disagreed once subjectStore has settled, regardless of which call site let them diverge in the first place.
designDecision.whyNotACleanroomRewrite: Replacing all five call sites' card-writing with pure derivation from subjectStore would eliminate the P-60 'instant pending card' UX (thin identity card painted before the sheet seals) and touch a much larger, high-traffic surface for a single-lane bug-fix scope. The additive reconciliation subscription preserves the existing pending-card UX untouched (subjectStore never holds a pending/thin sheet -- only sealed ones -- so the reconciliation only ever fires with a fully resolved, correct card) while making the SEALED state's agreement an enforced invariant instead of a five-way convention.

falsifiersPreRegistered: If the fix only changes the refusal message text or suppresses/softens the export-target check, the detector is hidden and the defect kept -- NOT what this fix does; export-target.ts is untouched.

If the brief renders correctly but the export target is still settable independently of the brief, the two can still diverge -- GUARDED: the export's expected id is cardNodeId, which the reconciliation now forces to equal subjectStore's id whenever they disagree; there is no remaining path for the two to diverge and STAY diverged once subjectStore is set.

If reconciliation ever fires on a null/unset subject, an inspected-but-not-yet-selected card would be wrongly blanked -- GUARDED: reconcileCardWithSubject returns null (no-op) whenever subject is null, matching subject-store.ts's own AMENDMENT 1 ('the previous subject stands' on an unplaceable or not-yet-sealed resolve).
